question: Using Section 9E.12 and Figure 9E-12, state the minimum bicycle-box length, required pavement symbol, turn-on-red rule, and green-pavement coverage rule.
model_answer: Direct Answer: A bicycle box must be at least 10 feet long (measured from the upstream edge nearest the motor-vehicle stop line to the downstream edge nearest the crosswalk or intersection), and at least one bicycle symbol marking must be placed inside the box. Turns on red are mandatorily prohibited from the lane where a bicycle box is placed. Green-colored pavement in the box is optional, but if it is used, it must cover the full limits of the bicycle box (green pavement itself being restricted to specific bicycle-facility applications, including bicycle boxes). Standards (mandatory): - "If used, the distance from the upstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest to the stop line for motor vehicles to the downstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest the crosswalk or intersection shall be at least 10 feet. At least one bicycle symbol marking (see Figure 9E-12) shall be used in the bicycle box." - "Turns on red shall be prohibited from the lane where a bicycle box is placed." (Section 9E.12 Standard §09, shown on the page view [Image 3].) - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box." (Section 9E.12 Standard §13, shown on the page views [Image 1]/[Image 4].) - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be limited to: … E. Bicycle Boxes (see Section 9E.12) …" Options (permitted): - A bicycle box may be used to increase the visibility of stopped bicycles on the approach to a signalized intersection during the red signal indication for motor vehicles in the approach lane(s) behind the box. - "Green-colored pavement may be used in a bicycle box." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 1) illustrates a bicycle box across one lane with the "10 ft MIN." dimension between the advance stop line and the intersection stop line, bicycle symbol markings inside the box, and the label "Green-colored pavement (optional)." - [Image 2] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 2) shows a bicycle box across multiple lanes with the NO TURN ON RED (R10-11) sign posted at the approach, the "10 ft MIN." dimension, and countdown pedestrian signals required where the box crosses more than one lane. - [Image 3] The Section 9E.12 text page shows Standard §09, "Turns on red shall be prohibited from the lane where a bicycle box is placed," and the 10-foot/bicycle-symbol Standard §06. - [Image 4] The full page for Figure 9E-12 Sheet 1 includes Standard §13: "If used, green-colored pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box." - [Image 5] The Section 3H.06 page shows the Standard limiting green-colored pavement to specific bicycle applications, item E being "Bicycle Boxes (see Section 9E.12)." Citations: - Section 9E.12 Standard §6 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §1 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §12 (p.1106) - Section 3H.06 Standard §2 (p.626) - Figure 9E-12 (p.1106) - Page 1146 - Page 1147 - Page 1148 - Page 666
gold_answer: The bicycle box must be at least 10 feet long, include at least one bicycle symbol, prohibit turns on red from its lane, and, if green pavement is used, fill the entire limits of the box.
